title: Ownership of Park Anaheim Healthcare Center in Anaheim includes 5 stakeholders as of June 2023
text:
In the first quarter of 2026, five stakeholders owned Park Anaheim Healthcare Center, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) data show. The facility, located in Orange County, has been under their ownership since June 30, 2023.
The current owners of Park Anaheim Healthcare Center are shown in the table below.
Park Anaheim Healthcare Center operates as a for-profit nursing home.
At that time, the facility’s overall CMS rating stood at two, which falls below California’s state average of 3.2 for nursing homes. CMS ratings take into account inspection findings, staffing adequacy, and the quality of resident care.
The data indicate Park Anaheim Healthcare Center served an average of 106.6 residents daily during the first quarter of 2026, with a total of 115 available beds. The facility is not hospital-affiliated.
CMS records show Park Anaheim Healthcare Center had no fines or penalties in the first quarter of 2026.
Orange County, California, had 69 for-profit nursing homes in total.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate the country’s older adult population continues to rise as younger age categories decrease. Between 2020 and 2024, Americans aged 65 and older increased by 13%, while those under 18 decreased by 1.7%. Over the last century, the nation’s older population has expanded substantially, growing from 4.9 million in 1920 to over 61 million in 2024.
A study published in 2021 found that nearly half of Americans in this age group, or about 28 million people, could require long-term care and support services. The report also estimated that more than one-third may ultimately need nursing home care.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome, executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance, an insurance education group. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
